raw_response:
Well, let me sit down and think through this year, the way I always do.

---

I've been farming this little patch of land for fifty years now. Five and a half mu, that's all we've got — me and my wife, both getting up in years. Our son lives in town and sends a bit of money sometimes, but mostly we feed ourselves from this land and sell what we can. My back hurts in the morning but I can still do the work, just slower than before.

Stevia is what I plant the most of these days. The company — they come to the village, bring the seedlings in spring, and buy the dry leaves back in the fall. That way I don't have to worry about where to sell. My neighbor old Zhang started doing it six, seven years back and I followed him. I do about 3.5 mu of stevia. The rest, 2 mu, I keep in cotton. Cotton I've grown my whole life, my father grew cotton, I know cotton. I won't give it up.

For the stevia, the seedlings come end of April once the cold is gone. Before transplanting I plow with a small tractor — I pay the village fellow to come with his machine, can't manage that by hand anymore. Then I put down maybe a bag and a half of compound fertilizer per mu, that's about 75 jin, before I put the seedlings in. After the plants take hold and start growing, I'll topdress a bit of urea, maybe half a bag per mu. I water from the well right after transplanting, or the little plants die. Then another watering or two through the summer. We cut twice — once in July, again in September. My daughter-in-law comes from town for a few days at harvest to help, and we dry the leaves on the ground in the yard. Stevia doesn't have many bugs, mostly I just spray once for weeds early on.

Cotton I plant around the 20th, 25th of April, when the soil warms. I buy the seed from the agriculture shop — they say the new kinds don't come back true if you save them, so I buy every year. Same kind of fertilizer scheme — a bag and a half of compound per mu before planting, and some urea when the buds start showing. Cotton takes more spraying than stevia does, the bollworms come in July and you've got to spray three or four times or they eat everything. My eyes aren't so sharp but I can still mix the sprayer. I'll water maybe twice — once when the buds come, once at flowering. The picking is the hardest part, three or four passes from September into October. I hire a woman from the village to help pick, pay her by the jin. Last year I got about 230 jin per mu of seed cotton, not bad for an old man.

Total I'll spend maybe 3000 yuan on the whole thing — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, a little hired help. I don't like to spend more than I have. If the year is bad, I've still got the stevia contract and the savings for another season.
